items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Tesh was in that band called the Austin High Gang, which I think is -- I think there are some words about it in the Library of Congress, I am quite sure.

ctx.x: So just because the whole historical picture is interesting, so if you don't mind, while you are speaking of that, you said, since you had musicians are you talking about Frank Teschemacher, too?
I don't think Tesh started to drink that early. I met him at Austin High School, and I think we were about the same age again.

items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Frank Tesch Teschemacher and I were close, we went to Austin High School together, and we had -- I was still playing the C-Melody saxophone and we had a sort of sax team

ctx.x: mentioned Jess and what about Tesh. I mean, were you close with any of them?

Frank Tesch Teschemacher and I were close, we went to Austin High School together, and we had -- I was still playing the C-Melody saxophone and we had a sort of sax team and we would do -- were playing professionally now and getting as much as we could, we weren't really good enough to get -- to demand work, but Wingy Manone came to town and Wingy came right from New Orleans and he was the bandleader.
Wingy, you know, an interesting thing about him, he could get jobs, you know, he was a fairly good businessman, and terribly funny man, certainly one of the funniest men I have ever met.
